The showrunner finds the cuts and makes one shot per camera shot of your video, looks at each one, and decides from your request whether it changes and how many painted frames it takes. Before painting a frame it looks at who is in it and what each person is doing, and afterwards it checks the picture against that, painting it again when someone's size, place or expression was lost. A shot with nothing to change keeps your video's own frames, with no render. A shot too long for one render continues by itself. Splitting loses no quality and takes almost no space: each shot reads its part of your file, which is encoded again only if its frame rate differs from the model's.

The longer the video, the more likely qu: The longer the video, the more likely quality is to degrade over time: artifacts can accumulate and character identity may progressively drift. The effect is usually less visible when the generated video mostly preserves unmodified control-video content. If the model supports end frames, a useful way to limit drift is to prepare several end-frame images in advance with an image-generation model and assign them to successive windows. When generating sound with LTX-2, MiniMa: When generating sound with LTX-2, MiniMax H3 or Ovi, WanGP aligns each window's audio to the video timeline and replaces a short ending of the preceding soundtrack with newly generated overlap. This also applies to Continue Video: the source's ending may be replaced even if it came from another model or was never padded. Keep the model's default overlap; if WanGP reports that it is too short for audio repair, increase it to an allowed value. This prevents accumulated timing drift; Ovi still generates each window's sound independently, so sound or voice continuity is not guaranteed. MiniMax H3 generates a little sound past each window's last frame, so its windows join without replacing anything, and the videos it saves keep about 0.1 s of sound after the last frame: continuing such a video reuses its whole soundtrack. Players may show these videos 0.1 s longer, holding the last frame.
